c1.note: The Q3 2026 10-Q and earnings release both show 77.5 thousand period-end employees at Sept 30, 2026.

c2.note: The 77.5 figure is correct, but the employees row sits with the Credit Quality Metrics rows, which suggests Table 1 (Financial Summary) rather than Table 2; the table citation is probably wrong.

c4.note: The 10-Q shows 77.5 versus 76.3 at Dec 31, 2025, a 2% change; 'prior period' means the prior year-end.

c11.note: The 10-K shows 52.6 thousand at end of 2024 and 76.3 thousand at end of 2025, a 45% increase, following the Discover closing.

c13.note: The 10-K states that Capital One closed the Discover acquisition on May 18, 2025.

c15.note: Employees fell from 78.4 to 77.5 thousand quarter over quarter, shown as (1)%.

c16.note: Capital One's consolidated reporting is by Capital One Financial Corporation, which absorbed Discover in 2025, so the headcount covers the whole company; the passages do not state the count explicitly but confirm Discover integration.

c18.note: The 77,500 is dated Sep 30, 2026 (quarter-end) and rounded to hundreds, so it is not a live Nov 11 count.

c20.note: 77,500 at Sep 30, 2026 (76,300 at Dec 2025) falls within 76,000-78,000, so the range is consistent.

c19.note: The saved Q3 2026 10-Q has no headcount figure. Its only 'employees' mention is in forward-looking risk language, and 'associates' does not appear at all. The newer 77,500 figure (Sep 30, 2026) comes from S&P via stockanalysis.com, not a primary source. I did not check the earnings release exhibits

c1.note: Capital One's Q3 2026 earnings release and its 10-Q for the quarter ended Sep 30, 2026 both show period-end employees of 77.5 thousand, up from 76.3 thousand in Q4 2025. This is the latest reported figure as of the run date.

c18.note: Capital One reports headcount as a period-end figure in thousands to one decimal place, which rounds it to the nearest hundred. So 77,500 is the Sep 30, 2026 quarter-end count, not a live count for Nov 11, 2026.
